Baise|China.f: Deng Xiaoping helped lead the Baise Uprising here against the Nationalist government on December 11, 1929.

Wuzhou|China.f: A hub of the synthetic gemstone trade, specializing in corundum, spinel and cubic zirconia, sits where the Gui and Xun rivers meet.

Liuzhou|China.f: The Liujiang man, among the earliest modern humans found in East Asia, was discovered in a cave in nearby Liujiang County.

Hanzhong|China.f: Liu Bang was made lord of Hanzhong and later named his imperial dynasty after it, so the city gave its name to the Han dynasty.

Dali|China.f: The Chinese word for marble literally means Dali stone, a nod to the medieval kingdom's famous marble trade.

Taizhou|China.f: Geely was founded in Taizhou and went on to complete its acquisition of Volvo Cars in 2010.

Guangyuan|China.f: Wu Zetian, the only woman in Chinese history to rule directly as emperor, was born here.

Liupanshui|China.f: The name merges one character from each of its three counties: Liuzhi, Panzhou and Shuicheng.

Burqin|China.f: The county seat sits at the confluence of the Irtysh and Burqin River in the northernmost part of Xinjiang.

Baicheng|China.f: Baicheng means white town in Chinese, a translation of its Mongolian name Chaghanhot.

Wudalianchi|China.f: Its name means five great joint ponds, lakes formed after the Laoheishan and Huoshaoshan volcanoes erupted in 1720-21.

Fuyuan|China.f: This is China's easternmost county-level division.

Heihe|China.f: Aigun, now part of Heihe, was the capital of Heilongjiang from 1683 to 1690 before the capital moved to Nenjiang.

Jiamusi|China.f: Named Giyamusi in 1720, the city's name originally meant inn in the Manchu language.

Jiansanjiang|China.f: Asteroid 207723 Jiansanjiang is named after this farming region.

Jinzhou|China.f: It sits in the Liaoxi Corridor, which connects most land transport between North China and Northeast China.

Songyuan|China.f: The city sits on Jilin Oil Field, the sixth largest land-based oil field in China.

Yingkou|China.f: Foreign powers moved the Newchwang treaty port to the river mouth where Yingkou now stands because the river was too shallow.

Alxa Left Banner|China.f: Alxa Left Banner covers 80,412 square km yet had only about 2.5 people per square km in the 2020 census.

Arxan|China.f: Arxan National Forest Park offers a landscape of solidified lava formations, crater lakes and dense forests.

Huizhou|China.f: Exiled poet Su Shi renamed Huizhou's Feng Lake West Lake because it looked as beautiful as the one in Hangzhou.

Baoshan|China.f: Baoshan was once called Yongchang, and the Han dynasty set up Yongchang Prefecture here in 69 AD.

Lincang|China.f: Lincang is home to what is billed as the world's oldest cultivated tea tree, about 3,200 years old, in the village of Jinxiu.

Fuyang|China.f: A tomb holding bamboo-strip copies of the Yijing and Classic of Poetry was rediscovered in 1977 during airport expansion.

Jingdezhen|China.f: In 1855 Taiping forces destroyed all 9,000 kilns in this porcelain city, which were rebuilt after the war in 1866.

Longyan|China.f: Nicknamed the Home of Generals, Longyan had 68 natives made brigadier general or above in 1955 to 1968, 82% of Fujian's.

Shangrao|China.f: Shangrao's Wuyuan County is the hometown of Zhu Xi and Zhan Tianyou, the father of Chinese railways.

Wuyishan|China.f: The Wuyi mountain area has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999, recognised for both natural and cultural value.

Yichun (Jiangxi)|China.f: A Shang dynasty settlement, the Wucheng Site, was discovered in Yichun in 1973.

Mianyang|China.f: Mianyang's history spans over 2,200 years, since Emperor Gaozu of Han set up the first county here in 201 BCE.

Qianjiang|China.f: Qianjiang is nicknamed the Throat of Sichuan and Hubei because the Sichuan-Hubei and Sichuan-Hunan roads cross here.

Aksu|China.f: When Xuanzang visited in 629 CE, he recorded over 1000 Buddhist monks in the kingdom of Baluka, as the Aksu area was then known.

Hami|China.f: Legend says the Kangxi Emperor named the Hami melon after the Hami king who sent it to the Qing court as tribute.

Yining|China.f: Dzungar ruler Erdeni Batur founded the city as Khobak Sari, capital of the Dzungar Khanate, complete with a monastery.

Tengchong|China.f: Tengchong is the southwestern end of the Heihe-Tengchong Line, which splits China into areas of very different population density.

Tongliao|China.f: In 1924 Aikido founder Morihei Ueshiba was arrested by Chinese authorities in Tongliao and released into Japanese consular custody.

Xingyi|China.f: Wanfenglin's karst peak forest and Triassic marine reptile fossils about 240 million years old form a UNESCO Global Geopark here.

Xinyuan|China.f: Xinyuan was originally called Kunes and was renamed in 1946, the new name meaning New Headstream in Chinese.

Jiagedaqi|China.f: The name Jagdaqi comes from the Oroqen language and means area with Mongolian Scots pine.

Jixi|China.f: Jixi holds 780 million tons of graphite reserves, which rank first in all of Asia.
